# 11: Zellweger syndrome case study

A family is referred to clinical genetics with a severely ill new-born child who has received a clinical diagnosis of probable Zellweger syndrome. This is an autosomal recessive systemic disorder characterised clinically by severe neurologic dysfunction, craniofacial abnormalities, and liver dysfunction, and biochemically by the absence of peroxisomes. Zellweger syndrome is characterised by locus heterogeneity and can be caused by mutations in any one of several genes, encoding proteins known as pexins, which are involved in peroxisome biogenesis. In order to try and provide a genetic diagnosis, whole exome sequencing was performed in the family and variants in a known Zellweger gene, *PEX3*, detected:

| Gene | Position (GRCh37/HG19) | Genotype |        |                |
|------|------------------------|----------|--------|----------------|
|      |                        | Mother   | Father | Affected child |
| PEX3 | 6:143784092            | A/A      | A/G    | A/A            |
| PEX3 | 6:143792714            | G/TG     | G/G    | G/TG           |
| PEX3 | 6:143795928            | T/T      | T/A    | T/A            |
| PEX3 | 6:143800237            | T/C      | T/T    | T/T            |



::: {.callout-tip title="Test your understanding"}
- How would you format a VEP query for each variant?
- What are the predicted effects of these variants?
:::

You can invetsigate the variants furtehr in [gmomAD](https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org). Make sure to use the gnomAD version 2.1.1 so that GRCh37/19 is used and matches the genome coordinates you have been using in IGV. COmplete the following table:


|      |             |      | Observed | Global allele frequency | Number of homozygotes |
|------|-------------|------|----------|-------------------------|-----------------------|
| PEX3 | 6:143784092 | A/G  |          |                         |                       |
| PEX3 | 6:143792714 | G/TG |          |                         |                       |
| PEX3 | 6:143795928 | T/A  |          |                         |                       |
| PEX3 | 6:143800237 | T/C  |          |                         |                       |



In answering this question, remember that the impact of a variant on the gene product may or may not correlate with the effect size in terms of downstream phenotype. You’ll therefore need to use all the evidence available to you to predict whether variants you are seeing in the data might be causative of Zellweger syndrome or not.

::: {.callout-tip title="Test your understanding"}

- Have these variants been observed before in gnomAD?
- Which variants might be causative of Zellweger syndrome?
- How would you interpret these data in terms of providing a diagnosis and future risk assessment to the family?
:::
